speed_note: +1.54% against a +1.21% null control on byte-identical output, i.e. 0.33 points above the noise floor and not a measurable cost. That matches the mechanism: one metatype test plus one element-stride compare per symbol-mapped composite leaf, at print time. scripts.pipeline.timeit's own 7-repeat runs on this box returned -27.01% and +30.64% on consecutive invocations of the same two binaries, which is why the interleaved min with a null control is the statistic reported here
decisions: The filed hypothesis ('array lvalue emission may select element zero without preserving the 16-byte access width') is UPHELD verbatim, and so is the round-4 refuter's location: printc.rs's whole-array `name[index]` branch gates on `sym_off >= 0 && (sym_off % elsize) == 0 && st.get_size() > elsize` and never reads the access size.

The fix is one level ABOVE that branch, not in it. `push_partial_symbol_ir`'s top-of-walk whole-symbol break (upstream `pushPartialSymbol`, printc.cc:2033) is what hands a full-width cover to the caller in the first place; suppressing it for an array whose element stride is smaller than the access lets the existing artificial-field arm render the access, so the whole-cover and partial-cover spellings come from the same code path and cannot drift apart again.

The refuter's warning that a bare-name fallback is not enough is CONFIRMED and drove the design. Simply tightening the `name[index]` guard yields `v30 = v32;` and `v30 = 0;`, which is not valid C either (arrays are not assignable) and drops the width instead of stating it. `._0_16_` is the notation kuna already uses for `N bytes at offset M of this symbol` and appears four lines away in the same function as `v30._0_4_`.

A second defect the need did not file: the pre-existing rendering was INCONSISTENT, not merely wrong. The identical 16-byte whole cover printed a bare `v1` where the HighVariable's symbol offset happened to be -1 (gh275 `SUB168(v1,0)`, arraysubfield `return v1 << 0x40;`) and `v30[0]` where it was 0. Both now print `._0_16_`, which is why 3 of the 7 moved stage assertions are bare-name sites rather than subscript sites.

Seven pre-existing stage assertions were re-pinned, and each was inspected as emitted C rather than as a regex: `rodatastring #2` and `returncopysplit #5` are 8-byte writes into a `char[8]` that printed `v1[0]`/`v2[0]`, `undefname #8` is a TWELVE-byte read that printed `v3[0]`, and `ARRAYSUBFIELD #7` plus the three `GH275` rows are the bare-name variant. None of them is a behaviour the corpus was defending; `ARRAYSUBFIELD #7`'s comment explicitly documented the whole-container render as the part that was NOT fixed, and this is the part of it that is.

Default-on because the element-zero subscript is not a judgement call, it is a false statement about the access width; the option exists as the escape hatch for diffing against upstream Ghidra, not as a preference. Evidence for the flip: 0/675 datatest assertions, and a 40-image sweep in which every changed line is a token-for-token substitution.

The predicate is narrowed to TYPE_ARRAY with `element align size < access size`, and NOT to `access size > 1` or `access is the whole symbol`. A scalar, a struct and a union all keep the upstream break, and an access that fits inside one element keeps its subscript, which is what `elem()`'s `return g[3];` and the fixture's `return v2[3];` pin.

Not measured on the witness alone: the two `undefined16` locals in the corpus (`undefined16` is internally an undefined1[16] array) also pick up the suffix, which is the source of the 345 `._0_16_` tokens in the sweep. Read in context those are the good case, because they sit next to the `._0_8_`/`._8_8_` writes that built the value.
